question: Should OpenClaw adopt this PR’s shared localization-core package and localized Gateway/plugin metadata as the permanent cross-surface product contract, or should the work be narrowed into owner-approved slices?
rationale: The branch creates a new shared package and compatibility-sensitive presentation contract across several owner boundaries; code review alone cannot decide the durable API and rollout scope.

options.title: Approve the contract direction
options.body: Sponsor the shared package and additive metadata shape, then require current-head approval and client proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow into owner slices
options.body: Split the proposal into independently owned CLI/TUI, Control UI, Gateway/protocol, and plugin/channel changes with explicit contracts.

options.title: Defer the program
options.body: Pause this broad localization foundation until the RFC receives an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Approve the contract direction
recommendation.body: Sponsor the shared package and additive metadata shape, then require current-head approval and client proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The author is the only evidenced participant carrying the complete proposed contract; the appropriate core and surface owners should be added by maintainers.
